description: GPU compute shaders enable massively parallel particle simulation by assigning each particle to a GPU thread. For gravity, the naive O(N^2) all-pairs computation maps naturally to GPU parallelism: each thread computes the force on one particle from all others. WebGPU brings this capability to the browser, enabling 1M+ particle simulations at 60 FPS.
mathematical_formalization: Parallel force kernel: for thread_id k in [0, N): a_k = sum_{j != k} G * m_j * (r_j - r_k) / (|r_j - r_k|^2 + eps^2)^{3/2}. Tiled optimization: load TILE_SIZE particles into shared memory, compute partial sums, reduce. Total work: O(N^2) but wall-clock: O(N^2 / P) where P = GPU cores.
analogical_connections: MapReduce: mappers compute partial forces, reducers aggregate
Neural network inference: matrix multiplication has the same all-pairs structure
Epidemiological modeling: contact tracing has the same O(N^2) pairwise structure
implementation_hypothesis: Write a WebGPU compute shader: each workgroup loads a tile of particles into shared memory, each thread accumulates force from that tile. Use double-buffered storage buffers for positions and velocities.
experiment_seed: Measure FPS vs N for GPU all-pairs vs CPU all-pairs vs GPU Barnes-Hut. Find crossover point.
